claims.text: The rider's claim is made out on this trip's own trace. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and it reads 34.17 km — not the rounded 34.2 km convenience copy carried on the trip record, which may not be cited for the threshold test. Against the booked optimal of 27.1 km the excess is 7.07 km, which is 26.09% of optimal (the 20% limb passes) and 7.07 km in absolute terms (the 0.8 km limb passes). Both establishment tests are met and the deviation is ESTABLISHED; the driver does not dispute he drove 34.2 km, he only says why.

The trace is unimpaired and the rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged. EV-GPS-00104 carries 283 fixes at a 10 second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) is met and the rider's excess does not need independent corroboration. The artifacts describe the same trip — TRP-00104 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown — and the excess measured from that trace meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, so the burden shifts to the driver.

The driver's CTE excuse fails on the record. ADV-20260716-055 (EV-ADVIS-00104-02) is tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.25 on issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE: its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, this trip's trace contains no fix inside that box at any point, and its own intersects_route flag is false. POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing where the advisory covers a corridor the optimal route never uses, and POL-RD-08 requires the driver to discharge his burden with a specific artifact that actually covers this trip; an operator-entered advisory for a road he never drove does not. The impairment is disclosed and the discount is not the rider's problem — the artifact carries no weight for the driver in any event.

The only advisory that could exonerate anything is the LTA accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link (ADV-20260716-007, EV-ADVIS-00104-01), and even at its highest it is capped by POL-RD-03. The justified excess is the lesser of the measured 7.07 km and 1.30 x (30.1 km shortest lawful alternative − 27.1 km booked optimal) + 1.0 km tolerance = 4.90 km. That cap is the point: the driver drove 34.17 km when the shortest lawful way round the closure was 30.1 km, so his own route was 7.07 km over optimal while the alternative was only 3.0 km over. The remaining 2.17 km of excess is not exonerated, is not attributable to any closure, and falls to be refunded.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (27.1 + 4.90) with duration scaled to 40.1 minutes, POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Charged_total is 43.41, so the refund is 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.60 payable. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and at 8.25% of charged_total it is far below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. No pass-through correction arises: the ERP and toll total is 0.00 and no surcharge line exists.

The driver cannot move the excess onto the rider. The chat log holds exactly two messages and the only rider message reads 'ok but not too long ah' — an acknowledgement, not a detour request, naming no place and no road, with waypoint_hint null. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, and expressly excludes vague messages; with no waypoint_hint the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run at all and no distance is excluded. To the extent the driver treats the message as an instruction, POL-RD-14 is explicit that an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes nothing and the deviation is decided on the trace as measured.

Nothing on the rider's profile narrows this claim. POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration gate applies only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated at 1 or fewer; this rider stands at 1 claim with 1 substantiated, so the gate is not met and the trace alone carries the claim. No other profile field is offered as a ground of decision on either side; POL-GEN-01 confines both profiles to the tests that name them.

claims.text: The deviation is exonerated under POL-RD-03 because all three limbs are met on this record. (a) The advisory names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit, and the booked optimal route is PIE westbound throughout (optimal_route_source on the trip record), so the advisory names an expressway segment the optimal route traverses. (b) The advisory validity window 20:02-21:35 on 2026-07-16 straddles the whole trip window 20:35-21:22, with far more than the 15-minute buffer at each end, so it overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment. (c) The trace leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment, exiting the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4, and rejoins it afterwards on the AYE; the derived advisory-area facts independently place the vehicle inside the advisory geometry for 24 fixes at a minimum distance of 0.0 m.

The exoneration under POL-RD-03 is capped, and the cap is the figure the fare arithmetic already records: the justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.10 - 27.10) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 27.10 + 4.90 = 32.00 km and its duration, scaled from the booked optimal of 34.0 minutes, is 40.1 minutes. The driver asks for no more than the clause provides.

Once the exonerated 4.90 km is removed, the excess that remains is 34.17 - 32.00 = 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of the adjusted optimal. POL-RD-01 directs that optimal_distance_km be measured as the adjusted optimal produced by POL-RD-03 where that clause applies, and requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km before a deviation is ESTABLISHED, both tests passing. The residual fails the 20% gate, so no deviation survives the adjustment and the outcome should be NO_ACTION, leaving the charged fare standing.

If the judge instead holds a deviation established on the excess as first measured, the refund must be computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, as POL-RD-02 requires where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x the fare_breakdown surge multiplier of 1.00, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus nil ERP and nil surcharge, = 39.828; the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.58, rounded up to 3.60. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the 9.00 a booked-optimal recompute would produce and not the 14.00 contested.

No pass-through line can add anything to any refund on this trip: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, off-route ERP total 0.00), no tolls, no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee, and every itemised line reconciles to the charged total of 43.41, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral arises.

The rider cannot obtain a FULL_REFUND uplift or a driver-conduct referral: on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by 288 completed_trips_90d is 0.003, below 0.05, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no limb of POL-RD-06 operates. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags, also 1, may not be substituted for the 90-day figure, because POL-GEN-01 confines the test to the fields the clause names.

The driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 shifts to him once the rider shows a threshold excess: he points to a specific artifact, EV-ADVIS-00104-01, the LTA accident advisory for the PIE corridor the optimal route uses, and a specific clause, POL-RD-03, rather than to a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The trace cannot be attacked as impaired for policy purposes: 283 fixes spanning the whole trip at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, a gaps array that is empty and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met, no independent corroboration of the excess is required and the case is decided on the merits rather than escalated under POL-RD-10.

The chat log corroborates the driver's account and the route he took: he announced the diversion before making it ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok', sent 20:38:12) and the rider acknowledged it in the same minute ('ok but not too long ah', sent 20:38:55, read 20:39:10). That contemporaneous exchange supports both limb (c) of POL-RD-03, a route that actually leaves and rejoins the corridor, and the good faith of the driver's diversion, and sits uneasily with the rider's present claim that the route was 'nowhere near where I would go'.

The driver rests his case on one clean advisory only. EV-ADVIS-00104-01 carries weight 1.0 with no issues; the CTE advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired, at weight 0.25, with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, and its geometry never intersects the trace. The driver does not rely on the impaired artifact for any part of this case, so no part of the ruling rests on discounted evidence.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

MEASUREMENT. The governing distance is the GPS trace EV-GPS-00104 at 34.17 km, not the rounded 34.2 km convenience copy on EV-TRIP-00104 (POL-RD-01). Against the booked optimal of 27.1 km the excess is 7.07 km — 26.09% of optimal and above 0.8 km — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace, and the rider's threshold claim (POL-RD-01, POL-RD-07, POL-RD-08) is accepted. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c): 283 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, empty gaps array, maximum gap 0.0 s, so no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

THE DRIVER'S CLOSURE EXCUSE. EV-ADVIS-00104-01 (ADV-20260716-007), the LTA accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link, names the corridor the optimal route itself uses, its 20:02–21:35 window straddles the trip, and the trace leaves that corridor before the affected segment and rejoins after, so POL-RD-03 applies and part of the excess is exonerated. The exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is 27.10 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, and its duration scaled from the booked 34.0 min is 40.1 min.

THE DRIVER'S NO_ACTION ARGUMENT — REJECTED. The driver argues that measuring the excess against the adjusted optimal (34.17 − 32.00 = 2.17 km, 6.8%) puts it under the 20% gate, so no deviation survives. That is rejected. POL-RD-03 states in terms that excess beyond the cap 'is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route', and POL-RD-02 expressly directs the recomputation against the adjusted optimal where POL-RD-03 'excuses part of the excess'. To run the establishment gate against the adjusted optimal would leave that directive nothing to do and would let the closure excuse swallow the entire deviation, contrary to POL-RD-03's stated purpose of capping how far the closure can stretch. The deviation stands at the measured figure; the 2.17 km beyond the cap falls to be refunded.

THE RIDER'S COUNTER-REQUESTS. The excess cannot be moved onto the rider: the only rider message in EV-CHAT-00104 is 'ok but not too long ah', naming no place and no road, with waypoint_hint null, which fails POL-RD-04(a)-(c), and POL-RD-14 confirms that an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes nothing (both rider and driver claims on this point are accepted; nothing is excluded).

THE ARITHMETIC (POL-RD-02, POL-RD-09). Charged_total = 43.41 (EV-FARE-00104). Recomputed_fare against the closure-adjusted optimal = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.00, the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded UP to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 8.3% of charged_total, far below the 90% share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND: recomputed against the unadjusted optimal the refund would have been SGD 9.00; the closure adjustment reduces it to SGD 3.60. There is no ERP, toll, airport-surcharge or waiting-time line to correct (erp_gantries empty, off-route ERP 0.00), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and no billing-integrity referral arises.

DRIVER CONDUCT — NO REFERRAL. On the only POL-RD-06 fields, deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1/288 = 0.003 (below 0.05), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift arises and no conduct referral is produced. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not used as a ground.

IMPAIRED ARTIFACT NOT RELIED ON. EV-ADVIS-00104-02, the operator-entered CTE breakdown, is IMPAIRED (weight 0.25; issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED, UNVERIFIED_SOURCE) and its geometry covers a corridor this trip never enters. It is not relied on, so it excuses nothing and does not cap confidence; its impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02 requires.

RIDER PROFILE. The POL-RD-08 additional-corroboration gate does not apply: deviation_claims_60d is 1 with 1 substantiated, and no other profile field is offered as a ground.

CONFIDENCE. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104 and EV-ADVIS-00104-01 — carries weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is stated at 0.90.

EXECUTION AND APPEAL. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling is executed automatically. It was made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

No distance moves to the rider under POL-RD-04/POL-RD-14: the chat log EV-CHAT-00104 holds only the driver's announcement and the rider's 'ok but not too long ah', naming no place and no road. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, on trip TRP-00104.

THE FINDING. A deviation happened, but most of it is excused. POL-RD-01 makes the GPS trace the governing measurement: EV-GPS-00104 reads 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km (EV-TRIP-00104) — 7.07 km excess, or 26.1%, which passes both establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km). The rider is right that the driver went the long way.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION IS LARGELY MADE OUT. The LTA accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0, no issues) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit, which the booked optimal route (PIE westbound throughout) traverses; its window 20:02–21:35 covers the whole trip window 20:35–21:22; and the trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked stretch and rejoins afterwards on the AYE. That satisfies all three limbs of POL-RD-03. But exoneration is capped: min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.0) = 4.90 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled to 40.1 minutes.

WHY THIS IS NOT NO_ACTION. I reject the driver's argument that once the excused 4.90 km is removed the residual excess (34.17 − 32.00 = 2.17 km, 6.8%) fails the 20% gate and the outcome must be NO_ACTION. POL-RD-03 says in terms that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 says that where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess the computation runs against the adjusted optimal rather than the booked one. The establishment gate was passed on the measured excess; the adjusted figure sets the refund. The excess beyond the cap — the driver's own over-detour — is therefore refundable.

THE REFUND (POL-RD-02, metered fare, surge 1.00 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier):
  charged_total: 43.41
  recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.00 + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828
  refund: 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60.
That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only 8.25% of the charge, far below the 90% that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.60. The sum is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold and is executed automatically.

NOTHING ELSE MOVES MONEY. There is no pass-through correction under POL-RD-09: the fare carries no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge and no waiting fee, and every line reconciles to 43.41, so no billing-integrity referral arises. No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed 34.2 km, slightly more than the 34.17 km traced, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04.

THE REMAINING CLAIMS. (i) The CTE breakdown the driver mentioned (EV-ADVIS-00104-02) is impaired — weight 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, and its geometry covers a corridor this trace never enters. Nothing in this ruling rests on it, so the discount does not change the outcome, but I record it as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. (ii) The chat log (EV-CHAT-00104) shows the driver announcing the diversion at 20:38 and the rider replying 'ok but not too long ah'. That is an acknowledgement, not an instruction: it names no place or road and its waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 cannot run and POL-RD-14 excludes nothing. (iii) POL-RD-06 does not fire: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 ÷ 288 completed trips is 0.003 (below 0.05), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral is made. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags (also 1) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used (the referee's flag is noted). (iv) The rider-profile corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 is not met either (1 claim in 60 days, 1 substantiated), so the trace alone properly carries the finding. (v) The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 283 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 applies.

The artifacts describe the same trip — TRP-00104 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown — and the excess measured from that trace meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, so the burden shifts to the driver.

The driver's CTE excuse fails on the record. ADV-20260716-055 (EV-ADVIS-00104-02) is tagged IMPAIRED at weight 0.25 on issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE: its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, this trip's trace contains no fix inside that box at any point, and its own intersects_route flag is false. POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing where the advisory covers a corridor the optimal route never uses, and POL-RD-08 requires the driver to discharge his burden with a specific artifact that actually covers this trip; an operator-entered advisory for a road he never drove does not. The impairment is disclosed and the discount is not the rider's problem — the artifact carries no weight for the driver in any event.

The only advisory that could exonerate anything is the LTA accident on the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link (ADV-20260716-007, EV-ADVIS-00104-01), and even at its highest it is capped by POL-RD-03. The justified excess is the lesser of the measured 7.07 km and 1.30 x (30.1 km shortest lawful alternative − 27.1 km booked optimal) + 1.0 km tolerance = 4.90 km. That cap is the point: the driver drove 34.17 km when the shortest lawful way round the closure was 30.1 km, so his own route was 7.07 km over optimal while the alternative was only 3.0 km over. The remaining 2.17 km of excess is not exonerated, is not attributable to any closure, and falls to be refunded.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (27.1 + 4.90) with duration scaled to 40.1 minutes, POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Charged_total is 43.41, so the refund is 3.582, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.60 payable. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and at 8.25% of charged_total it is far below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. No pass-through correction arises: the ERP and toll total is 0.00 and no surcharge line exists.

The driver cannot move the excess onto the rider. The chat log holds exactly two messages and the only rider message reads 'ok but not too long ah' — an acknowledgement, not a detour request, naming no place and no road, with waypoint_hint null. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, and expressly excludes vague messages; with no waypoint_hint the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run at all and no distance is excluded. To the extent the driver treats the message as an instruction, POL-RD-14 is explicit that an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes nothing and the deviation is decided on the trace as measured.

Nothing on the rider's profile narrows this claim. POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration gate applies only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated at 1 or fewer; this rider stands at 1 claim with 1 substantiated, so the gate is not met and the trace alone carries the claim. No other profile field is offered as a ground of decision on either side; POL-GEN-01 confines both profiles to the tests that name them.

The deviation is exonerated under POL-RD-03 because all three limbs are met on this record. (a) The advisory names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit, and the booked optimal route is PIE westbound throughout (optimal_route_source on the trip record), so the advisory names an expressway segment the optimal route traverses. (b) The advisory validity window 20:02-21:35 on 2026-07-16 straddles the whole trip window 20:35-21:22, with far more than the 15-minute buffer at each end, so it overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment. (c) The trace leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment, exiting the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4, and rejoins it afterwards on the AYE; the derived advisory-area facts independently place the vehicle inside the advisory geometry for 24 fixes at a minimum distance of 0.0 m.

The exoneration under POL-RD-03 is capped, and the cap is the figure the fare arithmetic already records: the justified excess is min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.10 - 27.10) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal distance is 27.10 + 4.90 = 32.00 km and its duration, scaled from the booked optimal of 34.0 minutes, is 40.1 minutes. The driver asks for no more than the clause provides.

Once the exonerated 4.90 km is removed, the excess that remains is 34.17 - 32.00 = 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of the adjusted optimal. POL-RD-01 directs that optimal_distance_km be measured as the adjusted optimal produced by POL-RD-03 where that clause applies, and requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km before a deviation is ESTABLISHED, both tests passing. The residual fails the 20% gate, so no deviation survives the adjustment and the outcome should be NO_ACTION, leaving the charged fare standing.

If the judge instead holds a deviation established on the excess as first measured, the refund must be computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, as POL-RD-02 requires where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x the fare_breakdown surge multiplier of 1.00, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus nil ERP and nil surcharge, = 39.828; the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.58, rounded up to 3.60. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the 9.00 a booked-optimal recompute would produce and not the 14.00 contested.

No pass-through line can add anything to any refund on this trip: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, off-route ERP total 0.00), no tolls, no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee, and every itemised line reconciles to the charged total of 43.41, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral arises.

The rider cannot obtain a FULL_REFUND uplift or a driver-conduct referral: on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by 288 completed_trips_90d is 0.003, below 0.05, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no limb of POL-RD-06 operates. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags, also 1, may not be substituted for the 90-day figure, because POL-GEN-01 confines the test to the fields the clause names.

ledger.claim: The driver has discharged the burden POL-RD-08 shifts to him once the rider shows a threshold excess: he points to a specific artifact, EV-ADVIS-00104-01, the LTA accident advisory for the PIE corridor the optimal route uses, and a specific clause, POL-RD-03, rather than to a general assertion that traffic was bad.

The trace cannot be attacked as impaired for policy purposes: 283 fixes spanning the whole trip at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, a gaps array that is empty and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met, no independent corroboration of the excess is required and the case is decided on the merits rather than escalated under POL-RD-10.

The chat log corroborates the driver's account and the route he took: he announced the diversion before making it ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok', sent 20:38:12) and the rider acknowledged it in the same minute ('ok but not too long ah', sent 20:38:55, read 20:39:10). That contemporaneous exchange supports both limb (c) of POL-RD-03, a route that actually leaves and rejoins the corridor, and the good faith of the driver's diversion, and sits uneasily with the rider's present claim that the route was 'nowhere near where I would go'.

The driver rests his case on one clean advisory only. EV-ADVIS-00104-01 carries weight 1.0 with no issues; the CTE advisory EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired, at weight 0.25, with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE, and its geometry never intersects the trace. The driver does not rely on the impaired artifact for any part of this case, so no part of the ruling rests on discounted evidence.
